q.t: Matter is made of…
o: A very large number of extremely small particles
q.e: Too small to see even with an ordinary microscope.

q.t: The gaps between particles are called…
The forces holding particles together are…
Which has a definite shape AND definite volume?
Which has definite volume but no definite shape?
q.e: Particles move within a limited space.

q.t: Which has neither definite shape nor volume?
Liquids and gases together are called…
Ice melts at…
Who first proposed the idea of Parmanu?
Heating makes particles move…
q.e: That explains melting, boiling, evaporation and diffusion.

q.t: Ground chalk powder is still chalk. Grinding is a…
Sugar dissolved in water can't be seen because…
o: It broke into particles too small to see
q.e: The particles spread through the water.

q.t: In solids, particles can only…
q.e: Strong attractions hold them in place.

q.t: A high melting point means…
Evaporation happens…
o: At any temperature, at the surface
q.e: Boiling is at boiling point, throughout, fast.

q.t: Why can a gas be compressed but water can't?
o: Gas particles have lots of space between them
q.e: Liquid particles are already close together.

q.t: Potassium permanganate spreads fastest in…
q.e: Faster particle motion in hot water.

q.t: Incense fragrance fills a room because…
o: Air particles constantly move and spread it

q.t: Smoke spreading from jar A into empty jar B shows gases…
q.e: Negligible attractions let particles move freely.

q.t: Moving your finger through water and it closes behind shows liquids…
Sugar dissolves and the water level drops back. This proves…
o: There are spaces between water particles
q.e: Sugar particles slip into the gaps.

q.t: Sand in water raises the level and stays raised because…
o: Sand doesn't dissolve and takes up space
q.e: It settles rather than filling interparticle spaces.

q.t: What is in the space between particles of a solid?
Ice floats on water because…
o: Ice's particles are farther apart than water's
q.e: Ice is an exception to the usual rule.

q.t: Why doesn't sand dissolve in water?
o: Its particles are held too strongly for water to pull out
q.e: Water can't pull its particles apart.

q.t: Which has maximum interparticle spacing?
Urea melts at 133 °C and ice at 0 °C. Which has stronger interparticle forces?
How does soap clean oil?
o: One end attaches to oil, the other mixes with water
q.e: Oil is lifted off and washed away.

q.t: SPM in pollution reports means…
q.e: 'Particle' means different things in different contexts.

q.t: What determines the physical state of matter?
o: The thermal energy of the particles

q.t: Why can you pile sand but not water?
o: Sand is solid; water's particles move freely

q.t: How does invisible air add weight to a balloon?
o: Air is matter — its particles have mass

q.t: Which three are true of liquids?
o: Definite volume, take container's shape, practically incompressible

q.t: Even a slight increase in interparticle distance makes the attraction…
A gas jar of iodine vapour shows violet spreading into an empty jar. This demonstrates…
Arrange by interparticle attraction, highest first:
q.e: Strongest in solids, negligible in gases.

q.t: Boiling happens…
o: Throughout the liquid at the boiling point

q.t: Water particles pull potassium permanganate particles out of the grain, then…
Why does a pressed syringe of air spring back when released?
o: The compressed gas particles push back

q.t: Which observation does NOT support 'particles are always moving'?
q.e: Grinding chalk shows small particles, not motion.
